dataflow.outcome: trusted-output spoofing and emulator-dependent terminal actions
dataflow.source: hostile document text, OCR text, commit message, or filename stored in a scope the operator inspects
dataflow.summary: stored text/metadata/path -> command response `Value` -> `print_output(..., json_mode=false)` -> raw `println!` or `eprintln!` -> interactive terminal

impact.why: The bug can spoof trusted CLI output, rewrite terminal display/title, create deceptive hyperlinks, and potentially request terminal-supported clipboard or control actions, but it does not itself execute shell commands or cross OS-user permissions.

likelihood.why: The trigger is a routine one-command human workflow once hostile content is present; there is no race or privileged prerequisite.

limitations: `--json` output is protected by JSON serialization.
Non-terminal sinks generally prevent terminal interpretation at command execution time.
High-impact OSC behavior depends on terminal policy.

reachability.entrypoint: default human-readable `kcs view`, `kcs log`, `kcs diff`, or `kcs status` output
reachability.outcome: operator-interface integrity loss in one terminal session
preconditions: The hostile string reaches one of the documented human-output fields.
The operator uses default human output in a control-sequence-aware terminal.
Terminal-specific actions stronger than display spoofing must be enabled by that emulator.

attackPath.summary: A lower-trust contributor places terminal-active bytes in a direct-child filename, indexed text or OCR output, or persisted commit message. The operator runs a routine human-readable command on that scope. KCS prints the string without terminal-safe escaping, so the interactive terminal interprets the bytes.

category: terminal control-sequence injection and output spoofing

codeEvidence.explanation: `run_view()` resolves an operator-supplied pointer and copies the selected stored chunk into the `text` field that the generic printer later renders.
codeEvidence.label: view places stored chunk text in command output

codeEvidence.explanation: The code validates chunk identity but then carries the stored `chunk.row.text` forward as ordinary text; it does not remove terminal-active controls.
codeEvidence.label: resolved chunk text is loaded from stored scope data

codeEvidence.explanation: `--json` output is the closest safe branch: JSON serialization emits escaped text instead of raw ESC/C0 bytes.
codeEvidence.label: JSON mode serializes and escapes control bytes

codeEvidence.explanation: Human `view` output forwards the lower-trust `text` string directly into `println!`, allowing terminal controls to reach the operator's terminal.
codeEvidence.label: human view output prints text verbatim

codeEvidence.explanation: Commit messages and repository relative paths receive the same direct terminal sink, so the renderer gap covers routine log, diff, and status views.
codeEvidence.label: human log, diff, and status output print metadata verbatim

codeEvidence.explanation: Any future lower-trust component embedded in `error.message()` would also bypass terminal-safe rendering in human mode.
codeEvidence.label: human error output has the same raw rendering shape

remediation.minimalFix: Replace direct `println!` and `eprintln!` interpolation for untrusted human fields with a shared `terminal_safe_text()` helper.
regressionTests: Assert that human output for `text`, `commits[*].message`, `changes[*].relative_path`, and `files[*].relative_path` contains no raw ESC, BEL, CSI, OSC, or bidi controls for synthetic inputs.
Assert that `--json` output remains valid JSON and round-trips the original logical strings.
Add a sibling test for human error messages that contain lower-trust components.
remediation.summary: Route every lower-trust human-output string through one terminal-safe renderer that visibly escapes C0 controls, ESC, CSI/OSC introducers, DEL, bidi controls, and hyperlink delimiters while preserving JSON semantics.

rootCause.summary: The violated invariant is that lower-trust strings displayed to a terminal must be visibly encoded before reaching `println!` or `eprintln!`. KCS applies JSON escaping for machine output, but the human renderer prints stored text, commit messages, relative paths, and sibling error text without an equivalent terminal-safe renderer.

summary: KCS serializes --json output safely, but default human-readable view, log, diff, status, and sibling error output paths print lower-trust text, commit messages, and relative paths directly to stdout or stderr. A hostile scope can therefore pass ESC/C0 or other terminal-active bytes into the operator's interactive terminal.
title: Human-readable CLI output emits untrusted terminal control sequences

assertions: Human `text`, `commit.message`, and `relative_path` branches interpolate strings directly into `println!`.
The safe synthetic observation found a raw ESC byte in the modeled human byte stream and no raw ESC byte in the JSON-encoded stream.
limitations: No live terminal control sequence was emitted.
Exact title, hyperlink, or clipboard effects vary by terminal emulator and policy.
No shell execution, OS permission crossing, or credential theft was established.
validation.method: V10 complete static untrusted-string-to-terminal trace plus non-emitting byte/JSON encoding control
validation.summary: Saved validation traced stored text, commit metadata, and relative paths into human output and confirmed that only JSON mode escapes control bytes. A synthetic ESC/BEL-bearing value was compared as hex and JSON escaped text without emitting the raw controls.
